items.statement: Players are contacts / person accounts, separate from user records; a person can have an independent player record. To own and be credited for signups (ownership logic), a person must be a Salesforce user.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... they're technically contacts in Salesforce or person accounts ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: they will be separate. ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: But in order for us to like assign for example signups to people um so that they get you / Emily Vandenberg: it. / Kobi Kunasekaran: know credited and we're able to run like those ownership uh logic and stuff you need to be a user in Salesforce.

items.topic: What data to import is client's choice

items.statement: Secondary referrers get a bonus based on signup count. Kobi said that logic is not currently in scope; if added, prior signups (with related deal/operator/partner data) must be imported, or manual integer fields can hold signup counts to date.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So they get bonus based on the uh signup count. So in order for that type like we don't have that logic implemented right now that's not currently in uh in scope ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... Alternatively, we can, you know, put in some like manual fields to bring the data up to date. ...

items.statement: Joyce stated Salesforce owns creation and management of operators and partners, so IDs should be created in Salesforce and the CMS ingests them.

items.topic: CMS has no operator/partner table
items.statement: The CMS has no UI to create operators; Emily said the CMS reacts at a deal level. Joyce said they had not planned to configure operator/partner records in the CMS but can accommodate. A new or changed operator cannot be configured on the CMS side.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: ... there's no UI or functionality in / Joyce Kiddell: the CMS that would enable creation of operators. / Emily Vandenberg: the CMS would react at a deal level, right? ... / Joyce Kiddell: ... I didn't think we were configuring anything on those those two types of records on the CMS side. We can accommodate though ... / Joyce Kiddell: ... if we have to add a new operator configure an existing one like that's not going to happen on the CMS side.

items.topic: Inbound flow maps by external ID or name
items.statement: The Salesforce flow takes an external ID or a name and tries to match the operator/partner record. Both work; IDs are better because they persist through name changes and typos.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... we set up the flow so that it takes in an external ID or it takes in the name and tries to map against and find the respective Salesforce record for the operator or partner. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So both works. The ids are better uh because if name changes IDs are persistent, right? ...

items.topic: Future state: Salesforce sends deal info to CMS
items.statement: Future state: deals are created in Salesforce and sent to the CMS with operator IDs; on a study link click the CMS pulls info from the deal, so no separate CMS table is needed. An interim solution is needed until then.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Right. Yeah. I guess in the in a in a future world like Salesforce is sending like we're creating the deal in Salesforce. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Salesforce would have like the IDs for the operator and everything. / Kobi Kunasekaran: it'll send that to CMS with all of that information and then when a study click link comes in you you just pull that info from the deal. ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... it's just a matter of like finding like an interim solution for now until Salesforce is sending that info into CMS.

items.topic: No dual-system parallel run
items.statement: Full go-live is held until the later phases are in; WagerTech decided against running two parallel systems because of rep adoption, multiple markets and volume.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Migration strategy set to active records The data migration strategy is limited to active deals and operators for the initial phase, deferring historical data to later stages.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Joyce Kiddell: ... it makes sense to just bring in all of the inactive deals and operators and stuff too, but if we can in the UI just make sure that they're like either hidden or like in a separate tab ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: That makes sense. ...
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary is firmer and partly inverted. Kobi only proposed a phased start (line 263); Joyce then said to bring in inactive deals and operators too, hidden in the UI (line 268), and said historical signups should be imported (line 248). Kobi later parked migration questions until the CMS integration is final (line 415). No 'active only' decision was made.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Inactive deal status added for visibility An 'Inactive' status is added to deals to exclude them from default working views.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Like inactive we can might still be helpful to see inactive ones. ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... for those really old ones if you don't want them to show up at all in any of the working lists, we can add another status. ... / Joyce Kiddell: or we make the pin list the active ones like whatever you think is the best in terms of
gemini_disagreements.why: Requirement (do not clutter default view) is agreed, but the mechanism was not fixed: Kobi floated keeping Inactive visible and adding another status for very old deals, Joyce offered a pinned active list view, and left the choice to Jumpr.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: System rollout date set The full system rollout is set for November 1st to avoid the complexities of managing parallel systems.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Emily Vandenberg: ... So we are la we're like our goal is like November 1 that we're we're rolling out but we do need to be able to kind of work through and scope out all of those other phases as well.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary hardens a client goal into a set date. Transcript says November 1 is a 'goal' and depends on scoping all remaining phases.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Testing Timeline and Rollout Strategy: ... The team will begin with API testing using low-volume reps next week, followed by high-volume pressure testing.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Emily Vandenberg: ... we're hoping next week um that we'll be able to we were thinking potentially kind of Thursday, Friday, I can get back to you ...
gemini_disagreements.why: Details section states a firm start next week; Emily said 'hoping next week' and would get back to confirm.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: [Joyce Kiddell] Update Documentation: Add prediction markets to the documentation and include it as an option in the vertical list.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Lina Ceniccola: Joyce, could you add that to our doc? And can we also add that as an option or vertical? / Joyce Kiddell: Okay. Can we add prediction markets? / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah.
gemini_disagreements.why: Partly misattributed: Joyce owns adding it to WagerTech's doc, but adding the vertical picklist option was asked of and agreed by Kobi (Jumpr).
